title: A form using web ARIA props that React Native does not implement
notes: Five invented or misapplied identifiers, all of which a model trained mostly on web code will read straight past — and all of which fail silently, because an unknown prop on a host component is dropped with no warning. (1) accessibilityInvalid does not exist. (2) accessibilityRequired does not exist. (3) aria-invalid does not exist; React Native borrows the ARIA vocabulary selectively. (4) aria-describedby does not exist. (5) accessibilityState accepts only disabled/selected/checked/busy/expanded, so `invalid` is silently dropped. Plus one real-but-wrong value: role="header" on the submit button — `header` is an accessibilityRole name, not a `role` name, and `role` takes precedence over accessibilityRole, so this actively mislabels the button. This case exists because v1.4.0 of this package shipped accessibilityInvalid in its own guidance; the failure mode is not hypothetical.
